content.content: When an open draft is discarded, the deccy CLI shall forget the draft's jj workspace, then remove the directory the draft's record handle derives under the per-user draft-workspace root and the repository's namespace — that directory and no wider path — and shall carry an absence at either point through as the same discard, neither refusing it because something is already gone nor reporting it as a success that removed what was not there.
content.rationale:
This node states, in the requirement form, the workspace half that vzposmvm carries for a discard and the open-draft end that slwvtspu carries, without adding an element either prerequisite leaves open. The trigger and the actor are slwvtspu's: an open draft is discarded and the deccy CLI ends it. The response names only what that end does to the two sides of the draft's workspace, because the record document, the change the workspace holds, brackets, markers and undo/redo are decided elsewhere and are neither restated nor moved here.

The sentence answers the three bearings the gate requires. The forget is the draft's jj workspace given up through the end of the draft, not a stop at the record or at the change: vzposmvm makes the forget the workspace seam's crossing, and the sentence names that operation while leaving the exact jj invocation, its arguments and its flags to the seam. The removal reaches the directory at the path the record's handle derives — the per-user draft-workspace root, then the repository's own namespace, then the handle with nothing appended — and confines itself to that directory and no wider path, so the namespace directory, the root and any path the handle does not give are untouched. The order is part of the same answer: the workspace is forgotten first and the directory removed after, because jj owns whether the workspace exists and removing the tree first would strip a working copy out from under a claim jj still holds.

The tolerance is one rule for the one end, not a policy per step. A draft whose workspace jj no longer holds, or whose directory is not there, is still ended: the discard is carried through as the same discard, neither refused because something is already gone nor reported as a success that removed what was not there. This keeps the seam's distinction between a workspace it dropped and one that was never there, and it does not turn the tolerance into a reconcile repair, a record rewrite, or the creation of a workspace to make a reference true.

The sentence adds no rule the prerequisites leave open: no order other than forget before removal, no path derivation beyond the per-user root, the namespace and the handle, no per-step absence policy, no drift repair, no record rewrite, and no verb surface — the command, its name, flags, arguments, output, refusal wording and exit status are unstated. The gate is review-criteria, so nothing runs; a reviewer reads this sentence against the two recorded prerequisites and reports any unanswered bearing or departed element by name.
